title: The Ship of the Desert
intro: You are going to read about camels and how they live in very hot and very cold places.

passage: For thousands of years, camels carried silk, spices and people along the Silk Road through Central Asia. Today you can still see them in the Kyzylkum Desert in Uzbekistan. People call the camel “the ship of the desert”, and it is easy to understand why. It can walk for days across hot sand with a heavy load on its back.

There are two main kinds of camel. The dromedary has one hump and lives in North Africa and the Middle East. The Bactrian camel has two humps and lives in Central Asia, China and Mongolia. Many people think that a camel's hump is full of water, but this is not true. The hump stores fat. When there is no food, the camel uses this fat for energy, and the hump becomes smaller and softer.

Camels are experts at living without water. In cool weather, a camel can survive for weeks without drinking. But when it finds water, it drinks very fast. A really thirsty camel can drink more than 100 litres in about ten minutes! That is almost a full bath of water.

The desert is a hard place to live, but a camel's body is perfect for it. A camel has two rows of long eyelashes, and it can close its nose. These protect it from the sand during a sandstorm. Its wide, soft feet don't sink into the sand. Bactrian camels also grow thick wool in autumn, so they don't feel the cold in winter. In spring, the wool falls off in big pieces.

Most camels today live with people. Families keep them in a herd and use their milk, meat and wool. But wild Bactrian camels are now very rare. Fewer than 1,000 of them live in the deserts of China and Mongolia. Scientists are working hard to save them, because the world would be a poorer place without these patient, clever animals.
